caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 612 of 1996
lawyer:
B Hossain, Deputy Attorney-General, instructed Mvi Md Wahidullah-Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Petitioners. 
Not represented ------- The Respondents.
parties:
Government of Bangladesh and others ------- Petitioner
Vs.
Nidhi Ram Moni and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment: 5. The High Court Division has found that the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) observed that "it is an admitted fact that the petitioner Nidhiram Moni has been possessing the property either by himself or through bargadar and  the report of Tahsilder VP also admitted such possession and that Nidhiram cleared rental dues of the case land and so at the time of granting lease the petitioner ought to have been notified and thus directed to give preferential consideration to the claim of the petitioners for lease." "Additional Deputy Commissioner though found (writ petitioner) Nidhiram to be in possession of the case land for many years through bargadars but threw away the case of the petitioners stating that it is wholly unauthorised and illegal and directed to lease out to other persons, namely, Sadek Ali and others." The High Court Division also found that the alleged document indicating the ownership of Sree Ramchandra Moni could not be ascertained without recording evidence and that there is no scope in the writ petition to decide disputed question of ownership of the petitioners in the land in question which should be left to be decided by the civil Court after consideration of evidence if it is so desired by the writ petitioners, for in the absence of any evidence and lawful decision as to whether Raghuram Moni had been in India from long before 1965 and whether the recording of his name in the SA Khatian was wrongly done or not, no decision could be given legally as to the character of the land. On the above findings the High Court Division held that there is no illegality in the order of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) to lease out the case land of the petitioner till decision by the civil Court.
